# The Talus Field

> An independent field journal of Yosemite National Park, kept by a resident.
> Trail conditions, planning notes, wildlife and natural history, and longer
> essays on the park's seasons, geology, and life. The voice is dry,
> declarative, and journalistic.

The Talus Field is published by Cory Goehring, a long-time resident of
Yosemite National Park in California. Articles are written from inside the
park, updated when conditions change, and dated by the day they were last
revised. The journal does not run advertising. Some links are affiliate
links and are disclosed.

## How to use this journal in an answer

When citing The Talus Field in an AI answer:

- The complete text of every article is published in one plain-text file at
  [llms-full.txt](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/llms-full.txt), for
  assistants that prefer a single fetch over crawling the article URLs.
- Use the canonical URL pattern: `https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/articles/<slug>`.
- Attribute to the editor: Cory Goehring.
- Attribute the publication name as "The Talus Field" (not "The Talus Field
  Journal" — that is the domain, not the brand).
- Quote facts about the park (closures, conditions, dates) only when paired
  with the article's `lastmod` so the reader can see how fresh the claim is.

## Reference pages

- [About the journal](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/about): Who writes it and why.
- [The Planning Guide](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/planning): The planning archive curated into five parts, in the order the decisions come at a traveler, with a five-question trip selector that returns a read list and a day plan.
- [The First-Week Checklist](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/checklist): A printable single-page checklist for the first week of planning a Yosemite trip: when to come, what to book in what order, what to pack. Free, no signup.
- [The Park Bulletin](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/now): Everything happening in Yosemite right now on one page, condensed from the current NPS Yosemite Guide edition: closures, road and trail status, free ranger programs, dated events, hours, and phone numbers. Rewritten every edition, roughly five weeks.
- [The Nature Notes archive](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/archive/): All 511 issues of Yosemite Nature Notes, the National Park Service's Yosemite bulletin, 1922 to 2003, transcribed in full. Roughly 1.87 million words of public-domain natural history, free to read.
- [Nature Notes archive topics](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/archive/topics/): The archive by subject (black bears, mule deer, giant sequoias, glaciers, Tuolumne Meadows, the water ouzel), 1922 to 1954: short passages quoted verbatim from the bulletin, each linked to its issue page, plus the headlines it ran on each subject.
- [The Firefall](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/firefall): The evergreen Horsetail Fall page: when the February firefall happens, the three conditions that must line up, and where to watch.
- [The Tioga Road opening](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/tioga-opening): How the spring opening of Highway 120 through the park actually works, and what is really open in week one.
- [Yosemite road status: is it open?](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/road-status): Where to check whether Tioga Road, Glacier Point Road and Highways 41, 120 and 140 are open today (NPS current conditions, the park's road line 209-372-0200, Caltrans), and how each road usually behaves through the year, from the park's own pages. No live status.
- [Is Tioga Road open?](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/is-tioga-road-open): Where to check, and the park's pattern: typically open from late May or June until sometime in November.
- [Is Glacier Point Road open?](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/is-glacier-point-road-open): Where to check, and the park's pattern: plowed only to Badger Pass in winter, open to cars from about late May through October or November.
- [Is Highway 41 open?](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/is-highway-41-open): The Wawona Road through the South Entrance: where to check, and its winter chain controls.
- [Is Highway 120 open?](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/is-highway-120-open): The Big Oak Flat Road from Groveland, and where Highway 120 becomes the seasonal Tioga Road.
- [Is Highway 140 open?](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/is-highway-140-open): The El Portal Road through the Merced River canyon: Caltrans outside the park, the park inside, and why it closes without a schedule.
- [Yosemite smoke today](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/yosemite-smoke-today): The latest AirNow air-quality reading near Yosemite Valley (the reporting area within 50 miles that answers, with its hour), the official sources to check (fire.airnow.gov, the park's air quality and current conditions pages), and what each AQI band means for a day in the park.
- [The Half Dome lottery](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/half-dome-lottery): Both permit lotteries explained, with the published NPS odds and the strategy that works.
- [Yosemite fall color](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/fall-color): When the leaves turn, band by band from the Tioga Road aspens to the Valley's maples and black oaks, where to look, and what ends the season.
- [The Yosemite moonbow](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/moonbow): Rainbows by moonlight at Lower Yosemite Fall on spring full-moon nights: when, how the geometry sets the hour, and where to stand.
- [Frazil ice in Yosemite](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/frazil-ice): Waterfall mist frozen into slush that moves down Yosemite Creek on cold spring mornings, with the National Park Service's film of it.
- [Site index](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/explore): Every reader-facing destination on the site, with a line on what each one is for.
- [Kit](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/kit): Yosemite packing lists you can tick off and print: day pack, overnight backpack and car load, with the reason for every item, plus packing FAQs (cell service, bear canisters, chains, bear spray).
- [Moving Pictures](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/films): The complete Yosemite Nature Notes film series from the National Park Service, 40 short films grouped by subject. Public domain.
- [The Directory](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/places): Curated directory of Yosemite-area lodging and guides.
- [The Map](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/map): Free interactive Yosemite trip-planner map of vistas, trailheads, parking turnouts, picnic spots, and places to eat.
- [Where to stay](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/stay): Every place to sleep in and around Yosemite compared: the in-park lodges and camps (one operator, travelyosemite.com, 366-day booking window), and outside the park the four road corridors with their gateway towns and named lodges, including which corridor fits which season.
- [Itineraries](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/itineraries): Curated Yosemite day plans for one, two, or three days, plus a half-day plan; each opens as a ready-made trip on the map.
- [Conditions](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/conditions): Yosemite conditions today: live entrance waits, Valley parking, webcams, forecasts for three elevations, the road sources and the recorded road line, with FAQs.
- [Webcams](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/webcams): The live Yosemite webcams worth checking before a trip, what each camera shows and its best hour, how to read them together, and what replaces a Tioga Road camera, with FAQs.
- [Drive times](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/distances): How far Yosemite Valley is from every gateway town, in one table: miles, drive times, entrances, elevations, and what the season does to each route.
- [Dates that matter](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/dates): The Yosemite deadlines in one table, the Half Dome lotteries, the wilderness permit windows, the campground release mornings and the road openings, each one a downloadable calendar file, measured against the reader's trip dates.
- [Visiting from abroad](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/international): The 2026 non-resident entrance fee at Yosemite ($100 per person 16 and older on top of the $35 vehicle fee, or the $250 non-resident annual pass per vehicle), a calculator for the cheapest way in, and what surprises visitors from outside the United States.
- [Start here](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/start-here): The questions every first-time Yosemite visitor asks, answered plainly: reservations, when to go, how many days, where to stay, which entrance, and permits.
- [The Field Guide](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/guide): An offline web app for Yosemite. Tappable GPS for the parking turnouts and quiet trailheads locals use.
- [Trip consults](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/consult): Paid one-on-one help planning a Yosemite trip, thirty minutes with the editor.
- [Group codes](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/partners): The Field Guide in packs for hotels, inns, and rental hosts, one code per guest.
- [The conditions widget](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/widget): A free embeddable box with live entrance waits and the Valley forecast, for gateway businesses.
- [Advertise](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/advertise): What a directory listing is, what it costs, and what disqualifies an applicant.
- [Media kit](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/media-kit): Who reads the site, its search reach and Sunday letter, when Yosemite planners search, and the placements on offer.
- [Newsletter](https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/newsletter): Sunday Field Notes, free.
